newsitem.title: USA: Janus fund manager had sought to buyout firm - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Janus fund manager had sought to buyout firm - WSJ.

text.p: Janus Capital Corp fund manager Tom Marsico's resignation earlier this week came after he had discussions with his boss about buying out the mutual fund company, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The paper said in its electronic edition that Marsico, 42, approached Janus chief executive and founder Thomas Bailey late last year about combining with him to buyout Janus, which is 83 percent owned by Kansas City Southern Industries.
But Bailey, who owns 12 percent of Janus, rebuffed Marsico's bid, the paper said. Tensions had then escalated between the two men ever since, the people told the paper.
Janus, if it were sold, may fetch between $1 billion and $2 billion, the paper said.
